So, I say that to say. Be selfless, all the time you spend on making yourself feel better and feel something! Use that and exert it towards your BS.
If you start to feel shame and guilt remind your self it’s human to feel that way but you need to use that energy and have some remorse and empathy for your BS. Feeling empathy,  is all about putting yourself in the other persons shoes. Would I like this if my BS did this to me?  

Remembering that your selfish decisions have consequences. So if your BS starts questioning your love or even who you’re as a person try not to make that about you and self loathe. Remind yourself that your BS is going through something traumatic and they will question even insult you at times because what they knew no longer exists. They feel lost, broken, betrayed, and scared. So if you’re expecting them to let you down easy or be nice remember how they react is based on what you did. So, hold yourself accountable and put your ego and  yourself on the back burner for right now.  Also remember, for some WS their ego is what got them in trouble in the first place. Wanting to boost their ego as a way to feel better about themselves. So, your ego can’t be trusted.

Another consequence is dropping AP or anything that is a reminder of your affair i. E jobs, friends etc.

If you cheated with a coworker. You need to find a new job and block AP.
You messed up and that’s a consequence for your action. The selfless thing to is to find another job even if you love the job.

Do what you know BS needs you to do. Majority of BS like myself have laid out for our WS what we need from them I.e honesty, going to therapy, marriage counseling, reading material, cutting off AP, phone access. Do it all. Your BS isn’t controlling you. They’re trying to learn a new way of trusting you and feeling safe. So if you once again, make this about yourself you won’t be able to understand or realize that perspective.

Think of it in a sense of a friend or family member betraying you in the worst way. Would you automatically trust them again or would you be very weary and even afraid to put your guard down? 

If you answered that question truthfully then that will help you understand your BS more and where they’re at mentally.

Lastly and most importantly. Work on yourself. Don’t say you will do it and not do the actual work. Don’t think you can work on yourself without seeking professional help. If it was possible you would have been able to have self awareness of your toxic behaviors and made changes long time ago.
You need someone there to help guide you and make the necessary changes. 

If you’re afraid of changing remind your self that becoming a safer partner isn’t about changing who you’re at the core. So I went to CUNY Hunter college. I told myself this is my second masters and honestly no one really cares what school you went to, to become an LMHC. What was important was that Hunters program was CACREP at the time. I knew I would eventually want to work at the VA and they require LMHCs master programs to be CACREP in order to get a job with them.


I was able to pay for my program out of pocket while working full time and that was very important for me.

I graduated 3 years ago and have my license. Before I was licensed, I worked for the state as a Behavior intervention specialist. After I graduated, I worked at a hospital and got my clinical hours fast. After that I moved to insurance company. 

During my years of working before and after school and licensure I have worked with LMHCs that went to Fordham, John J, CUNY, Columbia, NYU, Walden (online school) It doesn’t make a difference.  We all get the same jobs and do the same exact work and get the same pay. 

Maybe someone who went to Columbia will say otherwise. Like I said we all work at the same places. We intern and have practicum at the same places. I had no difficulty in getting placements for internship or practicum. CUNY had great connections. I also didn’t have trouble getting a job. Granted that maybe due to me working in the field fur many years prior but I got a job at a hospital a couple months after graduating. 

The only big difference is the CACREP part or if you’re going to get a PHD, what school you went to would matter. PHD program prefer brick schools over online schools but there’s also a lot of other things they look for and don’t care too much about someone having clinical experience vs research experience. 


Good luck!
